headline: Free Entry with Specific Activity and Train Reservations
reservation: General entry to Cuyahoga Valley National Park is free, but tickets for the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad must be booked separately via their official site. Lodging within the park is extremely limited; check availability for the Inn at Brandywine Falls through official channels or seek accommodation in Peninsula.

days.title: Waterfalls and Canal History

stops.name: Brandywine Falls
stops.detail: View the 60-foot waterfall from the boardwalk; arrive early as this is the park's most popular site.

stops.name: Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail
stops.detail: Walk or cycle a section of the historic trail near the Boston Store Visitor Center.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; the park is integrated with local roads and traffic.
days.note: Boardwalks can be slippery when wet; wear shoes with reliable traction.

days.title: Geology and Wildlife Marshes

stops.name: The Ledges
stops.detail: Hike the 2.2-mile loop through Sharon Conglomerate sandstone cliffs and shaded hemlocks.

stops.name: Beaver Marsh
stops.detail: Use the boardwalk on the Towpath Trail for birdwatching and spotting wetlands wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes between southern and central park areas.
days.note: Beaver Marsh is best visited at a slow pace for wildlife sightings; binoculars recommended.

days.title: Valley Rails and Rural Life

stops.name: Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad
stops.detail: Ride the heritage train through the heart of the valley; check official schedules for departure points.

stops.name: Hale Farm & Village
stops.detail: Visit this living history museum to see 19th-century life in the Western Reserve.

days.driving: Local transfer times vary; check specific train station departure times.
days.note: The scenic railroad operates on a seasonal schedule; tickets are required in advance.

intel.title: Brandywine Lot Congestion
intel.text: The Brandywine Falls lot often fills by 10 AM on weekends. Consider visiting late in the afternoon or on a weekday to ensure access.

intel.title: Variable Valley Coverage
intel.text: While near urban areas, signal drops in deep wooded ravines like The Ledges. Print maps for navigation between disconnected park parcels.

intel.title: Gateway City Services
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are abundant in Peninsula, Hudson, and Independence. There are no gas stations located directly within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Railroad Boarding
intel.text: Plan to arrive at train stations at least 30 minutes prior to departure. Boarding locations like Peninsula can be busy during peak foliage season.

intel.title: Towpath Conditions
intel.text: Check the NPS website for 'Eagle Nesting' closures or flood-related detours along the river. Sections of the Towpath may close temporarily after heavy rain.

plan.arrival: Fly into Akron-Canton or Cleveland Hopkins, rent a car, and head to Peninsula for a central orientation at the visitor center.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal; many park roads are narrow local routes through residential areas.
plan.goldenHour: Ledges Overlook offers a westward view over the valley canopy, ideal for sunset in autumn.
